title: Tuesday's page
how: Everything here passed my check and a blind reviewer's for obvious faults; the reviewer's remaining notes are beside each. Pick one per item; a note is optional. Your picks save on the page.
New today: one blind pair of Ron's voice acting. The rest is Monday's, not yet picked, except Sheila's voice as the game speaks it, taken off: a closer check found it leaning American for a moment.
Faces: front and profile in a plain studio light, and the face speaking a line.
foot: Anything you do not pick carries onto the next page.

sections.name: Ron, threatening: two ways of making his voice act
sections.note: The same line in Ron's voice, made two different ways, heard blind (which is which is kept off the page). Both passed the accent, words and likeness checks and a blind reviewer. Which sounds more like Ron meaning it? Only Ron's threat is here tonight: his other lines, and Sheila's and Darren's, failed the accent check in one way or the other.
sections.line: Walk away, son. Thirty years on the docks, and I never once had to ask a man twice.

sections.name: Sheila Dunn
sections.note: Her fifth face, shaped to the concept portrait by measurement. The blind reviewer's remaining notes: she reads about 45 to 48, not 53 (smooth forehead and upper lip, no smoker's lines); a peach tint on the upper lids and red inner corners; the hair darker and warmer than the concept's ash grey-brown; the proportions close to the concept. In the speaking frames her eyes blur during a blink. The haircut is Epic's nearest, not yet a set; her glasses come with her clothes.

sections.name: Darren Milner
sections.note: His fifth face, shaped to the concept portrait by measurement. The blind reviewer's remaining notes: the lids cut into the iris and the brows are heavy, so he looks sullen rather than quick and amused, and about 30; orange upper lids and red inner corners; the brown of the hair darker and redder than the concept's, the blond a band at the ends. The haircut is Epic's nearest, not yet a grown-out perm.

sections.name: The conversation light
sections.note: A faint light on whoever you are talking to, from above and to one side, and a catch-light in the eyes. It lights only their skin (not their hair), only that person, costs 0.2 ms a frame, and fades six seconds after they stop; a face already in sun gets none. Shown on Ron: judge the light, not the face.

sections.line: Forty years on the docks and they finished it with a letter. Mickey gave me the door. I don't forget that.

sections.name: Darren's voice, in the game
sections.note: His approved voice (Scottish, which the sheet notes), as the game speaks it. Carried from 25 September.
sections.line: A shape's not much to go on. Half the town could pass for that on a night like this.

sections.name: Ron, while he thinks
sections.note: When you ask him something, he says one of these at once, in his own voice, and stops the moment his answer starts. It covers the wait; there is no loading sign. Both of his, one after the other.

sections.name: Darren, while he thinks
sections.note: The same for Darren. Sheila has none yet: both tries leaned away from her accent.
sections.line: Hmm, well now.  /  Let me think.
